product.olivetti-m700-10.summary: Olivetti brought its MIPS workstation platform to the professional PC market.
product.olivetti-m700-10.history: Olivetti introduced the M700-10 in Paris in April 1992 as a high-end personal computer derived from its Cupertino PWS 4000 platform. MCmicrocomputer reported a list price just above US$14,000 for 16 MB of RAM, a 200 MB drive and a 17-inch monitor.
product.olivetti-m700-10.architecture: The expansion bus followed a high-end PC standard. The 64-bit MIPS R4000 was paired with EISA and up to 64 MB of memory.
product.olivetti-m700-10.verified: The configuration was checked against the cited sources. BluMach validation is pending.
product.olivetti-m700-10.limitations: The MIPS architecture requires its own CPU model. Board documentation, firmware, boot tests and a photograph with clear rights are pending.
